articles.title: England: Government “remains of the view” that the International Student Levy should go ahead; implementation planned for August 2028
articles.summary: The UK government confirmed in September 2025 that it will implement an International Student Levy of £925 per international student, to be charged as a flat fee to higher education providers. The levy is scheduled to take effect in August 2028, following its initial proposal in the May 2025 immigration white paper.
articles.insight:
The UK’s planned £925 International Student Levy—set for August 2028—may modestly dampen institutional competitiveness in price-sensitive source markets, though its direct impact on student demand remains uncertain pending final policy details and concurrent visa or scholarship adjustments.  
Admissions teams should track how UK universities absorb or pass on the levy, monitor shifts in application volumes from key regions like India and Nigeria, and assess whether rival destinations (e.g., Australia, Canada) position themselves as comparatively cost-effective alternatives ahead of the 2028 implementation.

articles.title: US colleges lost 20% of new foreign undergraduates, but one Southeast Asian country isn't budging
articles.summary: U.S. colleges experienced a 20% decline in new foreign undergraduate enrollments this year. Singaporean students, however, have remained relatively stable in their enrollment numbers in U.S. institutions.
articles.insight:
The 20% drop in new foreign undergraduates suggests broad demand softening—potentially tied to geopolitical concerns, visa processing delays, or shifting perceptions of U.S. value—but Singapore’s resilience hints that high-income, education-focused markets may remain less sensitive to macro trends.  
Admissions teams should track Singaporean application yield, scholarship uptake, and peer-market shifts (e.g., UK/Australia enrolment patterns), while reviewing messaging around safety, post-study work pathways, and institutional stability—not as an immediate pivot, but as contextual calibration for long-term recruitment strategy.

articles.title: Updated: US Department of Homeland Security publishes rule to end Duration of Status for international students
articles.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security published a final rule on 22 July 2026 to end Duration of Status (D/S) for F and J nonimmigrant students and their dependents. Despite extensive lobbying from scientific, business, and higher education sectors, DHS made only minor revisions to its original August 2025 proposal.
articles.insight:
This rule signals potential tightening of US student visa conditions, possibly dampening demand from risk-averse applicants in key markets like China and India, though actual enrolment impact depends on implementation details, alternative destinations’ policies, and how institutions mitigate perceived instability.  
Admissions teams should track early application trends for Fall 2027, consult legal advisors on updated compliance requirements, and assess whether messaging around visa predictability—especially versus UK/Australia’s streamlined pathways—needs refinement ahead of major recruitment cycles.
